description.to: The Pokémon's body is in a fluid, liquid state, causing physical blows to squish harmlessly through it — all damage from contact moves is halved. However, the bearer's liquid composition makes it especially vulnerable to Water-type moves, which are treated as super effective regardless of the bearer's typing (this effect stacks multiplicatively with existing type chart interactions).

to.effect: Multiply the final damage dealt to the bearer by 0.5. This applies after all other damage modifiers (type chart, stat stages, held items, etc.).
to.summary: Halve damage from contact moves
to.when: The incoming move makes contact (as defined by the contact flag)

to.effect: Apply an additional ×2 multiplier to the damage dealt to the bearer, stacking multiplicatively with the standard type-effectiveness chart. This represents the liquid body dissolving or destabilising when struck by Water. (Example: a Water move that would normally be neutral deals ×2; one that would normally be ×2 deals ×4.)
to.summary: Water-type moves are super effective against the bearer
to.when: The incoming move is Water-type

to: The contact-move damage halving applies only to moves that physically make contact; non-contact physical moves (e.g., Rock Slide, Earthquake) are NOT halved.
The Water super-effectiveness multiplier is independent of the bearer's actual typing. A Poison-type bearer normally immune or resistant to Water still takes the ×2 modifier from this ability.

If a move is both a contact move AND Water-type (e.g., Liquidation, Waterfall), BOTH effects apply: first halve for contact (×0.5), then double for Water (×2), yielding a net ×1.0 damage — the two effects cancel out exactly.
Ability-suppressing mechanics (Mold Breaker, Neutralizing Gas, etc.) remove both effects simultaneously.
This ability does NOT change the bearer's actual type chart for immunity purposes (e.g., a Water-immune bearer via Water Absorb would still trigger Water Absorb before this ability's modifier).

Cherrim's signature bloom ability. In harsh sunlight, Cherrim shifts from its Overcast Form into its radiant Sunshine Form (Fire/Fairy); outside of harsh sunlight it reverts to Overcast Form (Grass). Regardless of form, this Pokémon treats Fire-type and Grass-type moves as if they share its type, granting a flat 1.5× bonus to those moves — this ability-granted bonus does not stack with any natural STAB the user may already have from its own typing. Additionally, Morning Sun always restores 75% of maximum HP no matter the weather condition.

to.effect: If the bearer is Cherrim Overcast Form, transform it into Cherrim Sunshine Form. If the bearer is Cherrim Sunshine Form and harsh sunlight is NOT active, transform it into Cherrim Overcast Form. (Mirrors the existing hardcoded form-change keyed to ability ID flowergift.)
to.summary: Form flip: Overcast → Sunshine in harsh sunlight
to.when: Harsh sunlight is active when this Pokémon enters the field

to.effect: Re-evaluate form: if harsh sunlight is now active and bearer is Cherrim Overcast, transform to Cherrim Sunshine. If harsh sunlight is no longer active and bearer is Cherrim Sunshine, transform to Cherrim Overcast.
to.summary: Form flip driven by weather changes mid-battle
to.when: Weather changed to or from harsh sunlight during this turn

to.effect: Apply a 1.5× multiplier to the move's base damage. If the user's own typing already grants a natural STAB bonus on this move, this 1.5× does NOT stack — the move receives only the single 1.5× bonus (whichever source applies, the result is the same).
to.summary: Ability-granted STAB for Fire-type and Grass-type moves
to.when: The move being used is Fire-type or Grass-type

to.effect: Override the standard weather-dependent healing formula. Morning Sun always restores exactly 75% of the user's maximum HP, regardless of the current weather (including no weather, rain, sandstorm, hail/snow, or any other condition).
to.summary: Morning Sun heals 75% max HP regardless of weather
to.when: The move used is Morning Sun

to: The old team-wide 1.5× Attack and Special Defense boost to the user and allies in sun is FULLY REMOVED. That clause must not appear in any implementation.
The ability ID must remain 'flowergift' so the engine's hardcoded Cherrim form-change hook continues to fire correctly.

Cherrim Overcast is pure Grass-type. Cherrim Sunshine is Fire/Fairy-type. The ability-granted Grass STAB ensures that Grass-type moves such as SolarBeam, Petal Dance, and Magical Leaf receive the 1.5× bonus even in Sunshine Form when Cherrim is no longer Grass-typed. Symmetrically, Fire-type moves receive the bonus in both forms.

The non-stacking rule means a Cherrim Overcast using a Grass move gets exactly 1.5× (natural STAB equals ability-granted bonus — no doubling). A Cherrim Sunshine using a Grass move also gets exactly 1.5× from the ability (it lost natural Grass STAB). A Cherrim Sunshine using a Fire move gets 1.5× from the ability (it is not natively Fire-typed, so no conflict). If a future form or type-adding item somehow gives the bearer natural Fire-type, the bonus is still only 1.5× total.
This ability mirrors the design pattern of High Noon (STAB on Fire+Psychic, Morning Sun heals 75%) and Full Moon (STAB on Dark+Fairy, Moonlight heals 75%).
Morning Sun's 75% heal is unconditional — it cannot be suppressed by Cloud Nine, Air Lock, or any other weather-negation ability that would otherwise reduce the heal to 50%.
The form-change trigger should also fire any time the weather changes mid-battle (e.g., another Pokémon uses Sunny Day or the sun expires), not only on switch-in.
STUB — engine_hints ungrounded, needs human grounding pass

to.expect: Morning Sun restores exactly 75% of Cherrim's maximum HP, ignoring the sandstorm penalty entirely.
to.given: Cherrim Sunshine uses Morning Sun while Sandstorm is active (which normally cuts Morning Sun to 25% healing)

to.essentials: Rejuv (mkxp): patch/Mods/chrooked_corrosion.rb. ONLY the added damage clause is implemented; the vanilla poison-status-ignores-Steel/Poison clause is NATIVE in Rejuv and is left untouched. Poison-vs-Steel is 0x on the chart and Typemod multiplication cannot scale away from zero, so the multiply-by-(2/chart) trick used by excalibur/gastricsnare does NOT work here. Instead the handler rebuilds the Typemod slot by slot, substituting Typemod.new(2,1) for the Steel slot and PBTypes.oneTypeEff for every other slot. That rebuild needs the ATTACKER's ability as the key, so it required a NEW core table: CHROOKED_ABILITY_TYPEMOD in chrooked_00_core.rb, consumed in the pbTypeModifier prepend immediately BEFORE CHROOKED_MOVE_TYPEMOD. That ordering is load-bearing - ability-first lets a move-keyed override compose on top of the rebuilt value instead of being discarded by it. Guarded to atype == :POISON and targets with :STEEL, so non-Poison moves and non-Steel targets are untouched, and the global chart is unchanged for non-bearers. Not patched: Scripts/Battle_AI.rb still scores Poison moves against Steel using the vanilla chart, so the AI under-values them for a Corrosion holder. Rejuv's existing :CORROSION references (Battle_Inspect.rb line 10, Battle_AI.rb 454/9866/9867/9886) are all Corrosive-field scoring and are unaffected. Verified by references/rejuv-harness/typemod_check.rb (8 assertions, run with `ruby`).

to.effect: Check condition: (a) target has the SLP (sleep) status, OR (b) the user has the ability Daydreamer. If either condition is true and the target is not already under the Nightmare effect, apply Nightmare to the target. At the end of each subsequent round while Nightmare persists, the target loses 1/4 of its maximum HP. Nightmare is re-checked each end-of-round: it persists while the target is asleep OR a Daydreamer bearer opposes it, and clears otherwise. If neither condition is met, the Nightmare effect silently fails — the move still deals its damage with no additional message beyond a standard failure note.
to.summary: Attempt to apply the Nightmare residual effect after damage lands.
to.when: After damage is dealt and the target has not fainted.

to.effect: Target loses HP equal to 1/4 of its maximum HP (rounded down, minimum 1). This mirrors the vanilla Nightmare residual exactly; no new mechanic is introduced for the tick itself.
to.summary: Nightmare residual tick.
to.when: While the target has the Nightmare effect active.

to: Design intent: Dream Mist is the offensive, single-turn alternative to the vanilla Nightmare status move. Vanilla Nightmare costs a full turn and deals zero damage; Dream Mist deals 65 BP damage AND sets up residual in one action, at the cost of requiring the target to be asleep (or the user to have Daydreamer).

The Daydreamer ability gate is the key differentiator: only Musharna (or a future Daydreamer user) gets the unconditional payoff. Other users of the move (via Sketch, etc.) get a conditional payoff, keeping the move balanced.

The move is deliberately NOT a drain move. Musharna already learns Dream Eater at L40; making Dream Mist a drain would create redundancy. The residual is the unique value proposition, not HP recovery.
engine_hints is left empty per design spec; C citations and Essentials translation are a human pass.
STUB — engine_hints ungrounded, needs human grounding pass

Nightmare persistence is self-limiting and needs no new rule: the engine re-checks the sustain condition every end-of-round and clears the effect when it fails, so on an awake target the residual dies the moment the Daydreamer bearer leaves the field. See the daydreamer behavior spec.

to.expect: Move deals damage, Nightmare effect is applied. Target loses 1/4 max HP at end of that round and every subsequent round it remains asleep.
to.given: Target has SLP status, user does NOT have Daydreamer.

to.expect: Move deals damage, Nightmare effect is applied despite target not being asleep. Target loses 1/4 max HP at end of round.
to.given: Target is fully healthy, has no status condition, user has Daydreamer.

to.expect: Move deals damage only. Nightmare effect silently fails; no residual damage is applied.
to.given: Target has no status condition, user does NOT have Daydreamer.

to.expect: Move deals damage, but Nightmare is NOT reapplied (target already afflicted). Residual continues as normal.
to.given: Target already has Nightmare active, user has Daydreamer.

to.expect: Nightmare application step is skipped entirely (faint check precedes on-hit secondary effect).
to.given: Target has SLP status but faints from the initial 65-BP hit.

description.to: When this Pokémon enters the field it coils its body in preparation, loading a single strike. The very next biting move it uses is granted +1 priority — it lunges before opponents can react. Once that coiled strike is spent the charge is gone until the Pokémon switches out and returns, at which point the coil is reset. Flavor: a serpent slowly winding itself tight before snapping forward with terrifying speed.

to.effect: Set an internal flag COIL_UP_READY = true on the user. No visible stat change or message beyond the optional flavor announcement.
to.summary: Gain the coiled charge on entry

to.effect: Add +1 to the move's effective priority bracket for turn-order resolution only. Do NOT alter base move priority permanently. Then set COIL_UP_READY = false, consuming the charge.
to.summary: Grant +1 priority to the first biting move while the charge is active
to.when: COIL_UP_READY is true AND the move selected this turn has the 'bite' flag (i.e., is affected by Strong Jaw)

to: The charge flag should be stored per-slot (not per-species) so that Baton Pass / U-turn / Volt Switch sequences correctly reset it.

The priority boost applies at the turn-order calculation step, not at the accuracy or damage step — it does not interact with Taunts, Prankster, or Quick Claw in any special way beyond normal priority stacking.

If the user is forced to use a non-biting move while the charge is loaded (e.g., via Encore, Sleep Talk, Outrage lock), the charge is NOT consumed — it persists until a biting move is chosen voluntarily or the Pokémon leaves the field.
Moves that are redirected (e.g., by Follow Me) still consume the charge if the user's selection was a biting move.
Against Armor Tail / Queenly Majesty / Dazzling, the +1 priority bite is blocked as normal priority-blocking rules apply — the charge is still consumed on the attempt.
Parental Bond: if the user has both Coil Up and somehow Parental Bond, only the first hit inherits the priority bracket; internal consistency is handled at the engine level.
The ability interacts naturally with Strong Jaw (power) and does not double-dip — Coil Up only affects priority, not damage.
STUB — engine_hints ungrounded, needs human grounding pass

to.expect: Arbok's Crunch resolves at effective priority +1, so Arbok moves first despite equal base Speed or even lower Speed, then COIL_UP_READY is set to false.
to.given: Arbok (Coil Up) switches in. Opponent's Pokémon uses Earthquake (priority 0) on the same turn. Arbok selects Crunch (priority 0 base).

to.expect: Turn 1: Glare resolves normally, charge is NOT consumed. Turn 2: Crunch receives +1 priority (charge spent). COIL_UP_READY becomes false after Turn 2's Crunch.
to.given: Arbok (Coil Up) switches in. Turn 1 it uses Glare (not a biting move). Turn 2 it uses Crunch.

to.expect: On re-entry COIL_UP_READY is reset to true. The next biting move after re-entry again receives +1 priority.
to.given: Arbok (Coil Up) switches in, uses Crunch (charge spent). Arbok is then switched out and switched back in the same battle.

description.to: This Pokémon harnesses intense sunlight as a clean, self-sustaining energy source rather than burning through its own reserves. In harsh sunlight (including sunlight summoned by Drought, Desolate Land, or Orichalcum Pulse), this Pokémon's Special Attack is boosted by 1.5× — identical to Solar Power — but it does NOT lose HP at the end of each turn as a result of this ability. Outside of harsh sunlight the ability lies dormant, providing no stat modification. The ability is suppressed by Air Lock and Cloud Nine.

to.effect: Multiply the Special Attack stat by 1.5× before damage calculation.
to.summary: Boost Special Attack in harsh sunlight
to.when: Current weather is harsh sunlight AND this Pokémon is the attacker AND the move is a special move

to.effect: Skip any HP-draining side-effect that would normally be applied by Solar Power. This Pokémon takes no end-of-turn damage from this ability under any weather condition.
to.summary: No end-of-turn HP drain
to.when: Always (Solar Dynamo is active)

to.effect: No Special Attack modifier is applied and no HP is lost. Ability has no effect this turn.
to.summary: Ability dormant outside sunlight
to.when: Current weather is NOT harsh sunlight, OR weather is suppressed by Air Lock / Cloud Nine

to: Solar Dynamo is strictly Solar Power with its HP-drain drawback removed. It is intentionally stronger than Solar Power but weaker than Chlorophyll (which boosts Speed instead).
The 1.5× Sp. Atk boost applies only during harsh sunlight, making weather control (or a Drought teammate) essential for consistent payoff.
Air Lock and Cloud Nine suppress the weather, so Solar Dynamo becomes completely inert while those abilities are active.
Unlike the base Solar Power, this ability provides no penalty, so it pairs especially well with high Sp. Atk sweepers that would otherwise struggle to accept chip damage.
In doubles, a Drought setter + Solar Dynamo user forms a potent offensive core with no additional support needed to offset Solar Power's downside.
Desolate Land and Orichalcum Pulse both count as harsh sunlight and trigger the boost.
STUB — engine_hints ungrounded, needs human grounding pass

to.expect: The effective Sp. Atk is multiplied by 1.5× during the damage roll; no HP is deducted from the user at end of turn.
to.given: Solar Dynamo user with 150 base Sp. Atk uses Flamethrower under Drought-summoned harsh sunlight.

to.expect: The 1.5× Sp. Atk bonus is NOT applied, and no HP drain occurs. Ability is fully suppressed.
to.given: Solar Dynamo user is on the field while an opponent has Air Lock active. Sunlight would otherwise be harsh.

to.expect: The user does NOT faint from end-of-turn HP loss; it remains at 1 HP. The ability grants only the offensive bonus.
to.given: Solar Dynamo user survives to end of turn under harsh sunlight at 1 HP.

description.to: This Pokémon's body is saturated with a virulent, waterborne toxin that contaminates every drop of moisture it expels. Water-type moves used by this Pokémon have a 30% chance to poison the target (this chance applies even to targets that are normally poisoned only by Poison- or Steel-type Pokémon). Furthermore, any effect that would ordinarily inflict regular poison — whether from a move, this ability's Water-move proc, or a secondary effect — instead inflicts bad poison (toxic), making each instance of poisoning dealt by or through this Pokémon dramatically more debilitating over time.

to.effect: Roll a 30% chance. On success, inflict bad poison (toxic) on the target, bypassing the normal type restriction that limits poisoning to Poison/Steel interactions. This proc respects immunity to poison (e.g. Poison-type, Steel-type, Immunity ability holders) and cannot poison a target that is already statused.
to.summary: Water moves have a 30% chance to badly poison the target on hit.
to.when: The move used is Water-type and the target is not already statused.

to.effect: Intercept the poison status before it is written. Replace regular poison with bad poison (toxic), so the target begins accumulating escalating damage each turn instead of a flat 1/16 per turn. This upgrade applies to all moves and ability effects this Pokémon uses that can inflict poison (e.g. Poison Sting, Sludge, Poison Point contact proc).
to.summary: All poison applications made by this Pokémon are upgraded to bad poison.
to.when: This Pokémon is the source of a regular poison status being applied to any target (via move, ability secondary effect, or any other source).

to: The 30% Water-move proc and the upgrade-to-bad-poison effect are independent layers: the proc already inflicts bad poison directly, but the upgrade layer acts as a safety net to ensure no regular poison can slip through from any other source the bearer uses.
Standard poison immunities (Poison-type, Steel-type, Immunity, Pastel Veil, etc.) still block both effects entirely.
The ability does NOT grant immunity to being poisoned by the opponent — it only governs poison the bearer inflicts on others.
In doubles, the Water-move proc can trigger on spread moves (e.g. Surf, Muddy Water) against all targets hit, rolling independently for each.

Poison-type targets and Steel-type targets are immune to the proc despite the type-bypass clause (the bypass only waives the 'Poison/Steel users only' restriction on the user side, not the target's type-based immunity).
STUB — engine_hints ungrounded, needs human grounding pass

to.expect: Chansey is inflicted with bad poison (toxic), not regular poison. Its residual damage the following turn is 1/16 max HP, escalating each subsequent turn.
to.given: Bearer uses Surf against a Chansey (no status, no poison immunity ability). Roll returns 22 (under 30%).

to.expect: The status-apply upgrade layer intercepts the regular poison result and replaces it with bad poison before it is applied to Snorlax.
to.given: Bearer uses Poison Sting (a Poison-type move that normally inflicts regular poison on a 30% chance) against a Snorlax. Roll succeeds.

to.expect: The 30% proc does not fire — Poison-type targets are immune to being poisoned. Toxapex takes normal Surf damage only.
to.given: Bearer uses Surf against a Toxapex (Poison-type).

description.from: This Pokémon's body is saturated with a virulent, waterborne toxin that contaminates every drop of moisture it expels. Water-type moves used by this Pokémon have a 30% chance to poison the target (this chance applies even to targets that are normally poisoned only by Poison- or Steel-type Pokémon). Furthermore, any effect that would ordinarily inflict regular poison — whether from a move, this ability's Water-move proc, or a secondary effect — instead inflicts bad poison (toxic), making each instance of poisoning dealt by or through this Pokémon dramatically more debilitating over time.

description.to: On entry, hazards damage the user at neutral effectiveness, then all hazards on the user's side are moved to the foe's side.

to.effect: When calculating damage from type-based entry hazards (e.g. Stealth Rock), treat the incoming Pokémon's type(s) as having no weakness or resistance to the hazard's type. The hazard deals its base neutral fraction (1/8 max HP for Stealth Rock) regardless of type matchup. Non-type-based hazards (Spikes, Toxic Spikes, Sticky Web) are unaffected by this neutralization and trigger normally before the relocation step.
to.summary: Neutral hazard damage on entry
to.when: Stealth Rock or any type-based entry hazard is present on the user's side

to.effect: After all entry-hazard effects resolve on the user's side, every hazard layer present on the user's side (Stealth Rock, Spikes up to 3 layers, Toxic Spikes up to 2 layers, Sticky Web) is removed from the user's side and placed on the foe's side, capped at each hazard's natural maximum layer count on the foe's side. Layers that would exceed the cap on the foe's side are discarded. The relocation occurs once per switch-in and does not trigger the foe's own entry effects.
to.summary: Relocate all entry hazards to the foe's side
to.when: Any entry hazard(s) exist on the user's side after hazard-damage has been applied

to: Hazard damage and status application resolve before relocation; a Pokémon afflicted by Toxic Spikes on entry still receives poison before those spikes move.
The neutral-damage modifier applies only to type-based hazards. Spikes (flat % HP), Toxic Spikes (status only), and Sticky Web (Speed drop) are unchanged.
If the foe's side already has the maximum layers of a given hazard, relocated layers of that hazard are silently discarded.
Rapid Spin, Defog, and other hazard-clearing moves interact normally with relocated hazards on the foe's side.
Magic Bounce does NOT block Bioturbation's relocation — the ability is not a move, it is an ability trigger.
In doubles, 'user's side' and 'foe's side' refer to the respective team's full field side as normal.
If multiple Pokémon with Bioturbation switch in simultaneously (doubles), only one relocation resolves (last to be processed wins; implementation detail for engine pass).
STUB — engine_hints ungrounded, needs human grounding pass

to.expect: Walrein takes 1/8 max HP damage (neutral rate) instead of 1/4 (2× weakness). Stealth Rock is then removed from Walrein's side and placed on the foe's side.
to.given: Walrein (Ice/Water) switches into Stealth Rock. Walrein has Bioturbation.

to.expect: Sealeo takes 1/4 max HP from Spikes (3-layer flat damage, unchanged) and 1/8 max HP from Stealth Rock (neutralized). All Spikes layers and Stealth Rock then move to the foe's side.
to.given: Sealeo switches into 3 layers of Spikes + 1 Stealth Rock. Sealeo has Bioturbation.

to.expect: Hazard damage resolves normally (with SR neutralized). Stealth Rock moves to foe's side. The 2 Spike layers are discarded because foe's side is already at the 3-layer cap.
to.given: Foe's side already has 3 layers of Spikes. Pokémon with Bioturbation switches into 2 layers of Spikes + Stealth Rock on its own side.

description.to: Sound-based moves become Ground-type and gain +20% power. The user is immune to Ground-type moves.

to.effect: The move misses entirely; the user is immune to Ground-type moves.
to.summary: Ground immunity
to.when: The user is the target of a Ground-type move

to.effect: The move's type is changed to Ground before damage calculation. The move gains a 1.2× power multiplier. STAB applies if the user is Ground-type.
to.summary: Sound moves become Ground-type
to.when: The user selects a sound-based move

to: Type conversion happens before STAB; a Ground-type user using Hyper Voice would receive a 1.5× STAB on top of the 1.2× ability bonus.
The Ground immunity behaves like Levitate — the user floats above the sand — but is specific to this ability and is not classified as the Levitate ability itself.
Soundproof users are still immune to the converted Ground-type sound moves.
Moves that are both sound-based and already Ground-type (if any exist) receive only the 1.2× bonus; no double-typing occurs.
The immunity does NOT protect against Gravity-forced Ground moves or Smack Down interactions — those require separate engine handling.
STUB — engine_hints ungrounded, needs human grounding pass

to.expect: Hyper Voice becomes Ground-type, deals 1.2× its base power, and can hit Flying-types or Levitating foes only if they lack immunity to Ground (normal Ground immunity rules apply to targets).
to.given: A Pokémon with Singing Sands uses Hyper Voice against a target with no Ground resistance

to.expect: Earthquake misses/has no effect; the Singing Sands user is fully immune.
to.given: An opponent uses Earthquake against a Pokémon with Singing Sands

to.expect: Boomburst becomes Ground-type; Rock is not immune to Ground, so it deals neutral damage with the 1.2× bonus (Ground is not super-effective vs. Rock unless the target is also Fire, Poison, or Steel).
to.given: A Pokémon with Singing Sands uses Boomburst against a pure Rock-type foe

description.to: The Pokémon is only damaged by direct attacks. Passive damage from all other sources is negated.

to.effect: The damage and poison-on-entry effect from hazards are negated. The Pokémon still triggers Sticky Web speed drops (non-damaging effect).
to.summary: Blocks entry hazard damage
to.when: Stealth Rock, Spikes, or Toxic Spikes would deal damage or inflict poison on entry

to.effect: The residual HP loss from weather is negated. Weather-based stat boosts/drops are unaffected.
to.summary: Blocks weather damage
to.when: Active weather (Sandstorm, Hail/Snow) would deal end-of-turn damage to the user

to.effect: All such HP reductions are fully negated. Status conditions can still be inflicted; only their damaging tick is blocked.
to.summary: Blocks all other passive/residual damage
to.when: Any end-of-turn passive damage source would deal damage: burn, poison, bad poison, curse, binding moves (Wrap, Fire Spin, etc.), Leech Seed sap, or Nightmare

to.effect: Indirect contact-recoil damage (Iron Barbs, Rough Skin, etc.) and HP-drain reversal (Liquid Ooze) are negated. Standard move recoil (e.g. Double-Edge) is NOT negated — that is self-inflicted by the user's own move.
to.summary: Blocks indirect damage mid-turn
to.when: An effect that is not a direct attack move would deal damage (e.g. recoil from Rough Skin/Iron Barbs on contact, or Liquid Ooze)

to: Impenetrable is a functional clone of Magic Guard: it negates all damage that does not originate from a direct attack move targeting the user.
Status conditions (burn, poison, paralysis, sleep) can still be inflicted; only their damage ticks are blocked.
Sticky Web speed reduction, Intimidate, and other non-damaging effects are NOT blocked.
Standard move recoil from the user's own attacks (e.g. Double-Edge, Flare Blitz) is NOT negated, consistent with Magic Guard's canon behavior.
Life Orb recoil IS negated, as it is passive item-based damage, not a direct attack.
Leech Seed: the HP transfer is blocked on the user's side (no HP sapped), but the opponent does NOT receive the sapped HP since none is transferred.
Bad poison still ticks up its counter each turn even though no damage is dealt.
STUB — engine_hints ungrounded, needs human grounding pass

to.expect: User takes 0 HP from burn and 0 HP from Sandstorm; both damage ticks are fully negated
to.given: User with Impenetrable is afflicted with burn and stands in active Sandstorm at end of turn

to.expect: User deals damage normally and still takes the standard 1/3 recoil from Double-Edge; own-move recoil is not negated
to.given: User with Impenetrable uses Double-Edge (recoil move) against a foe

to.expect: No HP is lost from Stealth Rock on switch-in; the hazard damage is fully negated
to.given: User with Impenetrable switches in against active Stealth Rock (super-effective)

description.to: On entry, sets up Reflect and Light Screen on the user's side for 5 turns each.

to.effect: Apply Reflect to the user's side for 5 turns (8 turns if the user holds Light Clay).
to.summary: Erects Reflect on the user's side of the field upon switching in.
to.when: Reflect is not already active on the user's side

to.effect: Apply Light Screen to the user's side for 5 turns (8 turns if the user holds Light Clay).
to.summary: Erects Light Screen on the user's side of the field upon switching in.
to.when: Light Screen is not already active on the user's side

to: Both screens are applied in the same switch-in event; Reflect is applied first, then Light Screen.
Light Clay interaction: if the user holds Light Clay, both screens benefit from the extended 8-turn duration, identical to the behavior of the moves Reflect and Light Screen themselves.
Screen Cleaner and Defog still remove screens set by this ability normally.
If either screen is already present on the user's side when this Pokémon switches in, that particular screen is NOT overwritten or refreshed; only the missing screen is applied.
In doubles/multi battles, the screens protect the entire team side as normal.
STUB — engine_hints ungrounded, needs human grounding pass

to.expect: Both Reflect and Light Screen are immediately active on the user's side for 5 turns.
to.given: User with Dual Aegis switches in on a side with no active screens.

to.expect: Only Light Screen is applied; the existing Reflect is left untouched at its remaining turn count.
to.given: User with Dual Aegis switches in on a side where Reflect is already active but Light Screen is not.

to.expect: Both Reflect and Light Screen are active on the user's side for 8 turns.
to.given: User with Dual Aegis holds Light Clay and switches in on a side with no active screens.

to.effect: def_minus_1

description.to: A crushing electromagnetic blast. Super effective on Steel types and may lower Defense.

to.effect: If the target is Steel-type (primary or secondary), treat the Electric-vs-Steel matchup as 2x instead of the normal 1x. All other type interactions remain unchanged and stack multiplicatively, so a Steel/Ground target keeps its Ground immunity (0x overall).
to.summary: Type-chart override: this Electric move hits Steel super-effectively
to.when: The move resolves its type-effectiveness multiplier against the target's types

to.effect: Roll a 30% chance; on success, lower the target's Defense by one stage — the electromagnetic field physically warps metallic bodies and armor.
to.summary: Secondary effect: 30% chance to lower target Defense by 1 stage
to.when: The move successfully deals damage

to: Modeled on Freeze-Dry and the house move Excalibur: the move record reuses effect super_effective_on_arg with argument {type: Steel}; this spec exists to travel the mechanic to engines where that effect is not native (Essentials/Rejuv).
Steel/Ground keeps its immunity on purpose — Ground remains the counterplay to the trap-and-execute kit (Magnet Pull + Gauss Cannon).
Power stays at 80, below Thunderbolt, so matchup identity carries the move; vs Steel it plays like a 160-BP hit.
Flags [ballistic, pulse] follow the house cannon convention (Zap Cannon, Aura Sphere); pulse per author direction (Mega Launcher boost), ballistic means Bulletproof blocks it.
No contact — a field projection, consistent with the UFO/signal lore.

to.expect: Damage uses a 2x type-effectiveness multiplier (super-effective)
to.given: Gauss Cannon hits a pure Steel-type (e.g., Klink)

to.expect: 2x (Steel override) x 1x (Flying vs Electric is 2x in canon — combined per normal chart with the Steel override replacing only the Steel axis)
to.given: Gauss Cannon hits a Steel/Flying-type (e.g., Skarmory)

to.expect: Ground immunity is retained; 2x x 0x = 0x — the move has no effect
to.given: Gauss Cannon hits a Steel/Ground-type (e.g., Steelix)

to.expect: Standard 1x Electric-vs-Water effectiveness; no override applies
to.given: Gauss Cannon hits a pure Water-type

to.expect: Target's Defense drops by 1 stage after damage (secondary is type-agnostic)
to.given: Gauss Cannon hits any target and the 30% roll succeeds
